batches.why: Required and optional slots: a character without art for dance, sing, eat or think no longer does them, so its picks draw from a shorter table. Every trace here has at least one such buddy. The rest still come from the original engine.

A floor behaviour named directly in the air (happy, stand, sprawl) left a buddy hanging for good: only air falls, and nothing brought her down. She now lands first, then does it. Each of these recorded the hang, about 12,000 frames of it, so they are also shorter: settle no longer waits out its limit on a buddy who can't land.

Engine fixes from an artist's notes. Two of them move traces, and nothing else in these traces changes: frames, random draws, states and positions all match. A ceiling leap is no longer a throw: ceilGo set P.thrown so she could catch the ceiling, and now sets its own flag, so P.thrown reads false through the leap. 39 traces move there and only there, 6,451 pet frames, all in the air, thrown going from true to false. No buddy here has Thrown art, so nothing drawn changes. The swing's lean now follows her held art, not the frame's pose: with any of Held, swung left or swung right drawn it is a quarter of the swing all the way. The mixed buddy has only swung-left art, so she now leans a quarter where she leaned the whole swing, and stops jumping from one to the other at plus or minus 10. 12 traces move in that turn alone, 1,248 frames; resize-mixed is in both. Plain and full buddies lean as before.

Transitions from an artist's notes. One of the four moves traces: a timed state whose time runs out now lets her own art for the pose finish the pass it is in, at most one pass, when that art has more than one frame. With that change switched off, all 134 traces match as recorded, and in each of these 78 the first frame that differs is the first frame a timed state waits for its pass. No trace waits that isn't here. The full buddy draws 26 poses with one to four frames each, and the mixed buddy draws a three-frame walk and a two-frame hang, so their traces move; the plain buddy has no art and none of its traces move. 16,137 pet frames wait in all, most of them walking (6,357), then holding a wall, sitting, hanging, climbing and crawling. Everything after a wait follows from it: what comes next starts later and draws its random numbers later. The other three changes, a Roll pose, a stand up for each way down and the clips into Sit and Sleep, need art no golden buddy has, so they move nothing.

Quarter turns drawn over a few frames: going round a screen's corner, or catching a wall or the ceiling, she's drawn turning from the old facing to the new over 12 frames (longer for a half turn), her middle swinging round the corner point. Only the drawing changes. Played with easing switched off and on, every scenario has the same frames, random draws and buddy numbers on every frame, and in each of these 113 the first frame whose drawing differs is one being eased. No scenario eases without moving. Almost every run climbs or catches something; the 21 that don't stay as they were. Window corners ease too, but the maker has no windows, so they move nothing here.

A pickup drawn sliding: picked up, she's drawn first with the spot that was pressed under the cursor and her turn as it was, then slides to the usual hold over 10 frames. Let go during the slide, she falls from where she's drawn, and the rest of the slide carries on. Compared frame by frame with the trace before it, each of these 36 first differs on a frame being eased, within 12 frames of a pickup; every scenario with a pickup moves, and no other does. In all 36 the buddy numbers then differ from the first let-go during a slide on: the golden throws are quick, held 3 to 10 frames, so she falls from where she's drawn rather than from under the hold.

Drawn rising to the floor: let go with her feet under the floor line, she's on the floor at once as before, and drawn rising to it over 6 to 15 frames, 15 px a frame on average, with the landing as it was. Only the drawing changes: compared frame by frame with the trace before it, frames, random draws and buddy numbers match on every frame of all 134, and each of these 27 first differs on a frame being eased, within 18 frames of a landing. No scenario eases without moving.

A fix to the quarter turns above: into an inner corner, between a screen's wall and its ceiling, her middle was drawn swinging nearly a whole turn round the corner point to match the way she turns. It now takes the short way, as it barely moves there. All 36 are among the quarter-turn batch. Compared frame by frame with the trace before it, each first differs on a frame being eased while she climbs or crawls; frames, random draws and buddy numbers match on every frame, except in throw-plain-130, where she's picked up mid-turn and let go during the slide, so she falls from where she's drawn, as a pickup does.

Three corrections to the eased moves above, found by the per-hour probe. A pickup now starts from where she was last drawn, moved as far as the cursor since the press, not from where she was at the press, so one taken while she's moving doesn't jump: 31 of these first differ on an eased frame within 12 frames of a pickup. Leaving a surface mid-turn, the rest of the turn takes at least the time a turn that size takes: idle-mixed-44, acts-wall-plain and acts-wall-mixed first differ on an eased frame just after she left a wall or ceiling mid-turn. Rising to the floor goes at 10 px a frame on average, not 15: resize-plain and resize-mixed first differ on an eased frame just after such a landing. In 26 of the 36 the buddy numbers then differ, each from a let-go during a pickup's slide, which falls from where she's drawn; random draws differ in 5 of those, and only after it.

Review fixes to the eased moves. Let go during a pickup's slide, she now falls from under the hold as she always did, and is only drawn going on from where she was; with that, buddy numbers and random draws in all 134 traces match the engine from before any easing on every frame, so only the drawing differs. Played with each fix switched off alone against the engine with all of them, every one of these 110 moves for at least one fix, and each first differs from its trace before on a frame being eased: her middle is now taken through the whole drawing, the animation's own move, turn and scale included (moves 98); a plain move fades out the gap it started with, so the cursor or anything else carrying her moves her drawing all the way (65); a let-go mid-slide falls from under the hold, the only change to buddy numbers or random draws (36); a corner's swing keeps her box out of the surfaces it rounds, no deeper than she's drawn just before and after (77); a monitor that changes size stops a move under way (resize-plain, resize-full, resize-mixed). The winding a corner takes from its surfaces, not from her art's turn, moves none: the maker has no windows, and screen corners swing the short way.

Animation audit item 5 and its review fixes, on top of the eased moves: a roll on Stand rolls whole turns at the pace nearest hers within half to twice it, at least one turn, running at most a turn's time or a pass longer, and lands upright, unless walls keep turning her round: then the roll ends when its time is up, upright or not (a 240 px buddy on a 400 px screen can end about 38 degrees off). Leaving it out of the combined engine changes exactly these traces, all with a roll; they are the only traces whose buddy numbers or random draws differ from 2f8d99c's, each first at a frame where a buddy rolls.

Animation audit item 8 and its review fix, on top of the eased moves: poses centre on the middle of their pictures, moved by as much as the main image's art is off the middle of its own. Leaving it out of the combined engine changes exactly these traces, the full buddy's, whose boxes are off the middle.

Animation audit item 9 and its review fixes, on top of the eased moves: each run of an animation hands on from the values she was last drawn with over 8 frames, within one picture, surface frame, size and placing, mirrored on a turn round; Wave's sway ends at rest. The hand-on settles first and the eased move draws its final values. Leaving it out of the combined engine changes these traces. Item 6 changes none, and every trace that differs from anim-motion's recordings is in one of these three batches.

Review fixes to the eased moves, on the combined engine. Only the drawing changes: frames, random draws and buddy numbers match the trace before on every frame of all 134. Played with each fix switched off alone against the engine with all of them, every one of these 105 moves for at least one, and each first differs on a frame being eased: leaving a wall or the ceiling for the air is drawn turning upright over a few frames, kept clear of what she left (moves 97); her middle is taken through her art's own offset from the middle of its picture and her facing, so art drawn off-centre eases round a corner without a jump (52). A corner's path that would take her box off her monitors, the path carried along with a window that moves, and timing a path by her monitor's scale move none: the maker has no windows, one monitor at scale 1, and no path there leaves it.

An eased move ends when she comes onto a surface it wasn't heading for: landing mid-turn after leaving a wall or the ceiling, or after a throw, she's drawn as she stands from the tick she lands, not still turning on through the floor. Only the drawing changes: frames, random draws and buddy numbers match the trace before on every frame of all 134. In each of these 23 the first frame that differs is one the trace before was still easing and the new one has ended the move.

Animation audit item 3's placing count, made the one count of placings on the combined engine: an animation's hand-on doesn't carry across any placing, not only a call or a find. Dropped in at the top from where she stood, a buddy whose standing and falling pictures are both her main image is drawn as she is there, not handing on from how she stood. Exactly these traces move, against the combined engine with the look's own count, each first at the frame of such a drop (frame 6019 and frame 880), and only for the hand-on's 8 frames each time: 16 and 12 frames in all. Leaving a wall or the ceiling is drawn as an eased move, so it isn't a placing and moves no trace.
